messages:
Sam: heads-up, running into a gap with trace_id linking for async workers — logs come into our ELK and traces go to OTLP/tempo. we lose the connection for background jobs. any lightweight patterns?
Leila: we ran into this in a spike. easiest is to inject trace/span into structured logs at the logging layer (logger adapter). add trace_id/span_id as fields. :+1:
Toni: example in Python logging adapter we used: 
```py
logger.info("task started", extra={"trace.trace_id": trace_id, "trace.span_id": span_id})
```
Sam: that helps for sync paths. tricky part is when jobs are enqueued with only an old header or none at all.
Devon: two pragmatic approaches: 1) persist trace context in the job payload when possible; 2) have the agent/collector enrich logs by extracting traceparent if present in headers and add normalized `trace.trace_id`.
Ingrid: also watch cardinality. If we index `trace.trace_id` on every log it explodes storage and makes retention cost huge. better to keep it as a non-indexed JSON field and only index when we explicitly need to query by trace.
Leila: agreed. for ES we keep fields non-indexed, and have a separate trace-link index (recent N days) that stores just (trace_id, timestamp, service, sample_tags) for quick joins.
Sam: nice. how are folks normalizing IDs? we have services emitting 64-bit vs 128-bit hex variants.
Toni: canonicalize to 32 char lower-hex (OTel semantic: 16 or 32 hex). we add a normalizer step in the collector: lowercase, left-pad or reject if malformed. stash malformed in `log.attributes._trace_raw` for audits.
Devon: also be mindful of sampling: if trace sampling drops spans, logs may still exist. don't assume presence of a full trace in the tracing backend. console UI needs to handle partial matches.
Ingrid: UX note — Redwood Console should show a "View trace" link on a log if we have a trace_id, and gracefully fall back to a partial trace view when only a subset of spans exist. show a badge: "trace partial". :eyes:
Leila: about OTLP collector config, here's a tiny filter-ish sketch we used: 
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
processors:
  batch:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: trace.trace_id
        action: insert
        value: ":unknown:"
exporters:
  logging:
service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
```
Toni: another option is to do tracing->log linking in the trace exporter — emit a lightweight trace-index event into a low-cost timeseries store (keyed by trace_id) so logs can join without paying ES index cost.
Sam: security/PII question: should trace_id ever be considered sensitive? some customers worried about exposing internal IDs externally via logs.
Devon: trace_id itself is not PII, but avoid embedding business identifiers in the same field. redact any user IDs. also add redaction rules in the log pipeline.
Ingrid: retention policy impact: if we plan to keep trace-link index 30d vs 90d, that changes cost for forensic queries. default 30d seems reasonable. add a tenant-level setting in Console for retention per org.
Leila: ops detail: we also add a `trace.resource.service` field on logs so Console filters are fast (`service: payments` + `trace.trace_id`).
Toni: small caveat: some open-source collectors truncate OTLP trace ids to 16 bytes for legacy compatibility. explicitly configure `preserve_trace_ids: true` in our collectors.
otel-bot: deploy pipeline: collector-config-v2 promoted to canary in us-east-1 at 08:12 UTC — will roll over 10% traffic.
Sam: thanks — for next step I'll prototype a collector attributes processor that normalizes trace ids and emits a small trace_index event. will post the PR.
Leila: happy to review. add a runbook snippet describing how to resolve mismatched lengths.
Devon: ping me if you want help designing the trace-index schema for cost efficiency.
Ingrid: and I'll draft Console UX mocks for partial-trace view + "open in tracing" flow.
Sam: cheers everyone :sparkles:
